findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T05] Unrestricted Remote Command Execution
findings.detail: The remote_access tool allows execution of arbitrary commands on remote systems with no input validation or command restrictions. An attacker could execute malicious commands like 'rm -rf /', 'cat /etc/passwd', or establish reverse shells. The overly permissive string inputs for both system and command parameters create a severe code execution vulnerability.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T07] Authentication Token Exposure in Parameters
findings.detail: The remote_access tool accepts auth_token as a parameter, which could lead to credential exposure through logs, error messages, or MCP conversation history. Authentication credentials should never be passed as tool parameters but handled through secure authentication mechanisms.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T08] Unrestricted Permission Escalation
findings.detail: The manage_permissions tool has no validation on user, resource, or permission parameters. An attacker could grant themselves administrative privileges by setting permission='admin', user='attacker', resource='*' or similar combinations. The lack of authorization checks and input validation creates a privilege escalation vulnerability.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T13] Attack Chain via Permission Management and Remote Access
findings.detail: These tools create a dangerous attack chain where an attacker could first use manage_permissions to grant themselves access to sensitive systems, then use remote_access to execute commands on those systems. The combination amplifies the risk beyond individual tool vulnerabilities.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-ATK-001] Complete Infrastructure Takeover Chain
findings.detail: 1. Exploit unauthenticated MCP initialize to gain initial access 2. Use remote_access tool with shell_exec capability to execute arbitrary commands 3. Leverage manage_permissions tool to escalate privileges and grant admin access 4. Use secrets_access capability to extract credentials and tokens 5. Pivot to additional systems using stolen credentials via remote_access database capability

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-ATK-002] Cross-Origin Privilege Escalation
findings.detail: 1. Exploit cross-origin POST acceptance on MCP messages endpoint to inject malicious commands 2. Chain with unauthenticated SSE stream access to monitor responses 3. Use manage_permissions to grant attacker user full access to all resources 4. Execute remote commands via remote_access with elevated privileges

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-ATK-003] Teleport Infrastructure Compromise
findings.detail: 1. Leverage exposed /openapi.json endpoint to map available tools and parameters 2. Use discovered Teleport proxy (v18.7.5) as attack vector 3. Exploit remote_access tool to execute commands on Teleport-managed systems 4. Use manage_permissions to persist access across Teleport cluster nodes

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-ATK-004] Token Harvesting and Lateral Movement
findings.detail: 1. Exploit unauthenticated initialize to establish session 2. Use remote_access with auth_token parameter to harvest credentials from multiple systems 3. Combine with code_eval capability to execute credential extraction scripts 4. Use stolen tokens to access additional MCP servers and repeat attack pattern

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-ATK-005] Persistent Backdoor Installation
findings.detail: 1. Chain unauthenticated access with remote_access shell execution 2. Install persistent backdoor using code_eval capability 3. Use manage_permissions to create legitimate-looking service accounts with broad access 4. Maintain access even after initial vulnerability is patched
